name: Linear
description: Work with Linear from Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot through Linear's official MCP server: find and update issues, plan projects, cycles and milestones, write comments and documents, and post status updates.
instructions:
This connector bridges **Linear's official remote MCP server** (`https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`), run by Linear. Linear's own server provides the tools: issues, projects, initiatives, milestones, cycles, documents, comments, labels, templates, status updates, releases, notifications and Linear diffs (code review). AnythingMCP puts them behind your MCP endpoint with OAuth for Claude and ChatGPT, per-tool roles, the audit log and response mapping, next to your other systems. Every tool gets the prefix `linear_`, so Linear's `list_issues` becomes `linear_list_issues` and never collides with another connector's tool of the same name.

**The tools come from the server.** At install AnythingMCP asks Linear's server which tools it has, so you get the set Linear serves today. Linear adds tools regularly: open the connector and click **Discover tools** to pick up new ones.

**Setup (about 2 minutes)**:
1. In Linear, open **Settings > Account > Security & access** and, under **Personal API keys**, create a new key. Name it after its use, for example "AnythingMCP".
2. Choose the key's permissions and team access. A key limited to read access gives a read-only connector; add write access (or only issue and comment creation) if the AI should change things.
3. Copy the key (Linear shows it once; it starts with `lin_api_`), paste it into `LINEAR_API_KEY` and install. It is stored encrypted and sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, which Linear's server accepts in place of its interactive sign-in.

**Safety**: the API key acts as the Linear user who created it. Everything the AI creates or changes appears in Linear under that person's name, and it reaches exactly what that person and the key's permissions reach. For a connector shared by a team, create the key from a dedicated Linear member with access to the right teams only. Switched off at install: the deletions (`delete_attachment`, `delete_comment`, `delete_diff_comment`, `delete_status_update`), `merge_diff` (merges a pull request or adds it to the merge queue), the `retire_*_label` tools (they change labels for the whole workspace) and `share_issue` / `unshare_issue` (they change who can see an issue). Turn one on per tool if the AI really needs it. For a strictly read-only connector, change the base URL in the connector editor to `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly`, which only ever exposes read tools, and click **Discover tools**.

**Working with it**: start with `linear_list_teams`, `linear_list_issues` (assignee "me" for your own issues) or `linear_get_issue` with an identifier such as ENG-123. Call `linear_list_issue_statuses` and `linear_list_issue_labels` before `linear_save_issue`, so status and label names match the team's. `linear_search_documentation` answers questions about Linear itself. A 401 at install means the key is wrong, expired or revoked; a 403 or a permission error on one tool means the key's permissions or team access do not cover it. Linear needs no IP allow list: the AnythingMCP server only has to reach `mcp.linear.app` over HTTPS.

LINEAR_API_KEY.label: Personal API key
LINEAR_API_KEY.help: In Linear: Settings > Account > Security & access > Personal API keys > New API key. It acts as you.
LINEAR_API_KEY.patternMessage: A Linear personal API key starts with lin_api_ followed by letters and digits. Paste the key alone, without "Bearer".

prerequisites:
- A Linear account in the workspace you want to reach; the key works with whatever that account can see.
- Personal API keys must be allowed in the workspace (admins can restrict them under Settings > Security).
- Network access from the AnythingMCP server to mcp.linear.app over HTTPS.

tools.name: linear_create_attachment
tools.description:
Deprecated fallback for tiny files only. Accepts base64 file content, verifies SHA-256 checksum, and uploads it through the MCP worker.
Prefer `prepare_attachment_upload` plus direct PUT plus `create_attachment_from_upload`.

CRITICAL: Do not print base64Content and then copy it into this tool call.
Opaque base64 copied through model-visible text is easy to corrupt.

Generate base64Content mechanically from the source bytes and pass it through a programmatic argument construction path whenever available. Before calling this tool, verify the values are consistent:

Unix-like shells:
file="/path/to/file"
base64Content=$(base64 < "$file" | tr -d '\n\r')
sha256=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
decodedSha256=$(printf '%s' "$base64Content" | base64 -d | shasum -a 256 | awk '{print $1}')
size=$(wc -c < "$file" | tr -d ' ') # optional; stat can also get file byte size
decodedSize=$(printf '%s' "$base64Content" | base64 -d | wc -c | tr -d ' ')

PowerShell:
$file = 'C:\path\to\file'
$bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($file)
$base64Content = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
$sha256 = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $file).Hash.ToLower()
$size = $bytes.Length # optional
$decoded = [Convert]::FromBase64String($base64Content)
$decodedStream = [IO.MemoryStream]::new($decoded)
$decodedSha256 = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -InputStream $decodedStream).Hash.ToLower()
$decodedSize = $decoded.Length

decodedSha256 must equal sha256. If you pass size, decodedSize must equal size.
Pass `sha256`. Passing `size` is optional, but recommended for clearer mismatch errors.

base64Content.description: Deprecated base64-encoded file content to upload

issue.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 hex digest of the decoded file bytes.

size.description: Optional expected decoded file size in bytes. Rejects the upload if it does not match.

tools.name: linear_create_attachment_from_upload
tools.description:
Link an already-uploaded Linear assetUrl to an existing issue as an attachment.

Use this only after:
1. prepare_attachment_upload returned an assetUrl and uploadRequest.
2. The client successfully PUT raw file bytes to uploadRequest.url.

This tool does not upload file content. It only creates the Linear attachment row.
If the direct upload failed or the signed URL expired, rerun prepare_attachment_upload and upload again.

assetUrl.description: Linear upload assetUrl returned by prepare_attachment_upload

issue.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

title.description: Attachment title. Defaults to filename or asset URL

tools.name: linear_list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Only valid together with `statusUpdateId`; omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

tools.name: linear_prepare_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Prepare a direct Linear file upload for an existing issue.

Workflow:
1. Call this tool with issue, filename, contentType, and size.
2. Upload raw bytes with PUT to uploadRequest.url outside MCP.
3. All headers in uploadRequest.headers are part of the signed request, so send them verbatim.
4. After PUT succeeds, call create_attachment_from_upload with assetUrl to link it to the issue.

Do not base64-encode or transform the file. Use curl --data-binary @path or fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: blob }).
Omitting or modifying any signed header, including casing, will return HTTP 403.
The signed URL must be used within 60 seconds or it will expire.

Upload sequencing:
Prepare, PUT, and finalize one file before calling this tool for another file.
Do not batch multiple prepare_attachment_upload calls before starting the PUTs because earlier signed URLs can expire while later files are prepared.

Example:
curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png \
  -H "content-type: image/png" \
  -H "x-goog-content-length-range: N,N" \
  -H "cache-control: public, max-age=31536000" \
  -H 'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="file.png"' \
  "<uploadRequest.url>"

contentType.description: MIME type, e.g. image/png or application/pdf

filename.description: Filename for the upload, e.g. screenshot.png

issue.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

size.description: Exact file size in bytes. Must be smaller than 2 GB.

subtitle.description: Suggested attachment subtitle for the finalize step

title.description: Suggested attachment title for the finalize step

tools.name: linear_save_comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`; comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string; use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Only valid together with `statusUpdateId`; omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

tools.name: linear_save_diff_comment
tools.description: Create, reply to, or edit a comment or persisted draft on a Linear diff. Set draft to true to save without submitting. Provide draftId to edit or submit a persisted draft, and commentId only to edit a submitted comment. Submitting an inline draft reuses its saved anchor; submitting a reply draft requires parentId again.

anchor.description: Optional comment anchor copied from a diff thread or built for a file or diff hunk

anchorContent.description: Exact source text of the anchor's end line; stored with an inline draft so it can be re-anchored after the diff receives new revisions

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string; use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences

draft.description: Save as a private persisted draft without submitting

draftId.description: Existing persisted draft ID to edit or submit

parentId.description: Top-level comment ID to reply to; also required when submitting a persisted reply draft

urlOrId.description: Linear review URL, diff slug, pull request ID, Linear full identifier, or GitHub PR URL

tools.name: linear_save_document
tools.description: Create or update a Linear document. If `id` is provided, edits the existing document; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `title` is required and exactly one parent (`project`, `issue`, `initiative`, `cycle`, or `team`) must be specified. On update, passing a parent reparents the document. To change parts of the content without resending all of it, pass `patch` instead of `content`.

content.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string; use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. When passing a name or number, also pass `team` to disambiguate.
